spoken_text: Imagine pointing a powerful laser at the moon.
reveal_opportunity: Moon rises into frame above the dome on "laser"

brief_visual_concept: Playful rejection of the wrong interpretation
spoken_text: Not to light it up.
reveal_opportunity: a lit-up Moon glow appears then is wiped away on "up"

spoken_text: To ask it a question.
reveal_opportunity: a question mark forms from the pulse-marker dots on "question"

spoken_text: You fire a pulse
reveal_opportunity: single pulse leaves the aperture exactly on "pulse"
transition_opportunity: cut to Earth-Moon schematic after pulse clears frame

spoken_text: at a reflector sitting on the lunar surface.
reveal_opportunity: ring marks the landing region on the Moon on "reflector" (a ring and dot only, NOT the hardware: the answer comes at B17-B18)
transition_opportunity: match cut: ground view -> schematic Earth-Moon view (Moon stays on the same screen spot)

spoken_text: Now, how long before that light comes home?
reveal_opportunity: stopwatch (0.00 s) fades in on "how long"

spoken_text: About two and a half seconds.
reveal_opportunity: stopwatch freezes on 2.56 s on "seconds"; digits show 2.56

spoken_text: Wait, that's there and back.
reveal_opportunity: a bold two-way arrow appears over the path on "and"

spoken_text: Not two and a half seconds each way.
reveal_opportunity: the "2.5 s" is split into halves on "each way"

spoken_text: A little over a second to reach the moon
reveal_opportunity: outbound leg counts 0 -> 1.28 s and the pulse lands on the Moon on "moon"

spoken_text: and a little over a second to return.
reveal_opportunity: return leg counts 1.28 -> 2.56 s, pulse reaches Earth on "return"

spoken_text: And because the moon's distance keeps changing,
reveal_opportunity: Moon slides along an exaggerated elliptical path on "keeps changing"
transition_opportunity: wipe to a top-down orbit diagram

spoken_text: the timing changes too.
reveal_opportunity: timer readout moves 2.38 -> 2.71 s as the Moon moves, on "changes"

brief_visual_concept: Visual pause and change of focus
spoken_text: But hold on.
reveal_opportunity: everything holds still on "hold"

spoken_text: Why would the light come back at all?
reveal_opportunity: a faint pulse reaches the Moon and does nothing (scatters dark) on "come back"

spoken_text: Did someone leave a mirror on the moon?
reveal_opportunity: a mirror silhouette ghost appears and is questioned on "mirror"

spoken_text: Actually, yes.
reveal_opportunity: dashed mirror is replaced by the real reflector assembly on "yes"
transition_opportunity: match cut to the lunar-surface sequence

spoken_text: Apollo astronauts left special reflectors on the lunar surface.
reveal_opportunity: astronaut walks in and sets the array on "left"

spoken_text: Their corners have a clever trick.
reveal_opportunity: camera pushes into one corner cube and the housing becomes a cutaway on "trick"

spoken_text: They redirect a tiny fraction of incoming light
reveal_opportunity: a ray enters, reflects off the faces, exits on "light"

spoken_text: back toward where it came from.
reveal_opportunity: exit ray lines up with the entry ray on "from"

spoken_text: Back on Earth,
reveal_opportunity: cut to Earth on "Earth"
transition_opportunity: hard match cut: reflector ray -> telescope ray

spoken_text: a telescope looks for the return.
reveal_opportunity: telescope aims at the Moon and a detector lights on "return"

spoken_text: And here's the really strange part.
reveal_opportunity: light dims on "strange"

spoken_text: Almost none of the light makes it back to the detector.
reveal_opportunity: beam footprint widens on its way to the Moon and again on the way back; return glow shrinks on "none"

spoken_text: Scientists have to collect just a few returning photons
reveal_opportunity: single detector click marks appear on "photons"

spoken_text: from many laser pulses.
reveal_opportunity: pulse counter ticks up and dots stack into a histogram on "pulses"

spoken_text: A few photons.
reveal_opportunity: three individual dots light and hold on "few photons"

spoken_text: They even account for the effects of Earth's atmosphere.
reveal_opportunity: atmosphere layer blurs/bends the beam on "atmosphere"

brief_visual_concept: ADDED from the recording: faint returns let them measure distance
spoken_text: And somehow those incredibly faint returns let them measure the distance
reveal_opportunity: dots on the histogram resolve into one clean peak on "returns"

spoken_text: with remarkable precision.
reveal_opportunity: precision readout appears on "precision" (number only after C10 is sourced)

spoken_text: So how does it work?
reveal_opportunity: everything simplifies to the plain Earth-Moon line on "work"
transition_opportunity: clean wipe to the model view

spoken_text: A cosmic stopwatch.
reveal_opportunity: stopwatch shown with a cosmic backdrop on "stopwatch"

spoken_text: Take the round trip time,
reveal_opportunity: round-trip bracket labelled "t" on "time"

spoken_text: multiply it by the speed of light,
reveal_opportunity: c x t builds and the full path length bar appears on "light"

brief_visual_concept: Separate two-way path into one-way distance
spoken_text: then divide by two.
reveal_opportunity: path folds in half on "two": the bar halves, one leg remains

spoken_text: That's your distance.
reveal_opportunity: distance value appears on "distance"

spoken_text: The moon isn't just hanging in the sky.
reveal_opportunity: camera pulls back to a wide shot as the Moon is shown in space on "hanging"

spoken_text: With each faint return,
reveal_opportunity: one last faint return arrives on "return"

spoken_text: we can measure where it is.
reveal_opportunity: ruler value settles on "is"
